The image shows a corn ear peeled open revealing a dark black/sooty mass inside, with dried brown husks. This is a pod/ear issue. Key candidates from the pod/seed part index: Head_Smut, Common_Smut, Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Gibberella_Disease, Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, Aspergillus_Ear_Rot.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with the most likely candidates.
Head_Smut reference shows a dark spore mass inside the ear with dried brown husks, very similar to the test image. Let me check Common_Smut next.
Common_Smut shows distinct white/silvery galls on the ear, very different from the test image. Let me continue checking other candidates.
Diplodia shows white mold on kernels, not matching. Let me check Gibberella, Trichoderma, and Aspergillus.
Gibberella shows pink/red mold on husks, not matching. Let me check Trichoderma, Aspergillus, and get another Head_Smut view.
Trichoderma shows dark green/gray mold on husk exterior, not matching. Let me check Aspergillus and another Head_Smut reference.
Aspergillus shows olive-green powdery mold on kernels, not matching. Let me view another Head_Smut reference and also check Fusarium_Disease.
This Head_Smut reference is virtually identical to the test image. One more view needed to reach 8 classes.

Fusarium shows whitish-pink mold on individual kernels, not matching at all.

**Summary of 8 reference views across 8 classes:**
1. **Head_Smut** (pod/139) - Dark spore mass inside ear, very similar
2. **Common_Smut** (seed/218) - White/silvery galls, not matching
3. **Diplodia_Ear_Rot** (pod/27) - Moldy kernels visible, not matching
4. **Gibberella_Disease** (pod/64) - Pink mold on husks, not matching
5. **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot** (pod/24) - Green mold on husk exterior, not matching
6. **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot** (seed/15) - Olive-green powdery mold, not matching
7. **Head_Smut** (pod/206) - Virtually identical to test image
8. **Fusarium_Disease** (seed/25) - White mold on kernels, not matching

The test image shows an ear completely replaced by a dark black spore mass inside the husks, with no visible kernels. The Head_Smut reference (Corn_Disease_206.jpg) is nearly identical: same dark sooty spore mass filling the ear cavity, same dried brown husks peeled back. This matches the KB description of Head_Smut: "Large smut galls replace ears, first covered by fragile creamy white membranes that rupture to release masses of dark brown spores." The key differentiator from Common_Smut is that Head_Smut replaces the entire ear systemically, while Common_Smut forms discrete galls.
